constraints: New adapters live only in packages/agentic-system/src/local-git-workspace.js and packages/agentic-system/src/local-command-verifier.js and are exported from packages/agentic-system/src/index.js; backend-*.js and qa-*.js are not edited.
Every git and verification process is started with node:child_process spawn/execFile using an argument array and shell:false; no command string is ever interpolated.

Every test in the new file is titled with its criterion prefix (RB1..RB5 followed by a space), declares { timeout: 60000 }, creates its repositories under os.tmpdir() and removes worktrees and temp directories in finally blocks.

The model used by the end-to-end tests is a deterministic Core model adapter (defineModelAdapter-compatible generate()) whose next action is a pure function of request.observations; no network or provider credential is used.
Adapters are trusted local fixtures, not a sandbox; docs must say so and point isolation to BB-067.
Research only in this lane: no product source edits, no self-issued readiness or fabricated Jev judgment.
invariants: Backend ACCEPT through the local adapters requires a real commit in the isolated worktree and a PASS tests record executed at that exact commit.
A verification record is PASS only for an exit-0 process run at HEAD == candidate.version whose run left HEAD and the working tree unchanged.
The source repository HEAD, branches and working tree are never modified by Backend or QA runs.
Core, Oracle, completion policies and existing fake-based agentic tests are unchanged.
architectureDecisions: D1 — createLocalGitWorkspace({ repositoryRoot, baseRevision, worktreeRoot }) runs `git worktree add --detach <worktreeRoot> <baseRevision>` and returns { root, act, observe, head, dispose }. dispose runs `git worktree remove --force` and deletes worktreeRoot. baseRevision must be a full 40-hex commit that exists in repositoryRoot.

D2 — act({ candidate, action }) accepts action.kind === "APPLY_BACKEND_CHANGE" with action.edits [{ path, content }]. Paths must be relative POSIX, non-empty, without "..", drive letters, leading "/" or a ".git" segment, else it throws LOCAL_WORKSPACE_UNSAFE_PATH. It requires HEAD == candidate.version (else LOCAL_WORKSPACE_REVISION_MISMATCH), writes the files, runs `git add -A` and commits with fixed author/committer env (EXHARNESS_LOCAL_WORKSPACE identity, GIT_CONFIG_NOSYSTEM=1). It returns { mutated: true, candidate: { id: candidate.id, version: <new sha> }, result: { artifacts: [{ ref: `git:<sha>:<path>`, path }] } }. When `git status --porcelain` is empty after writing, it returns { mutated: false, candidate } and creates no commit.
D3 — observe({ candidate }) returns { candidate, head, files: <`git ls-files` at HEAD> } without writing.

D4 — createLocalCommandVerifier({ name, claim, root, command, args, timeoutMs = 30000, maxOutputBytes = 65536, requireUnchangedTree = true }) returns a Core verifier { name, verify }. verify({ candidate }) first requires `git rev-parse HEAD` in root == candidate.version, else FAIL with evidence reason REVISION_MISMATCH and no process spawned. It snapshots `git status --porcelain`, spawns command/args with cwd root and shell:false, and captures bounded stdout/stderr.

D5 — Status mapping: timeout → kill the process tree (POSIX: spawn detached and process.kill(-pid, "SIGKILL"); win32: execFile("taskkill", ["/pid", String(pid), "/T", "/F"])), then INCONCLUSIVE with reason TIMEOUT. Exit 0 → PASS; non-zero or spawn error → FAIL. When requireUnchangedTree and HEAD or porcelain status changed after the run → FAIL with reason TREE_MUTATED, overriding PASS.

D6 — Verification evidence is an array of strings: `${name}:revision=<sha>`, `${name}:exit=<code|null>`, `${name}:reason=<PASS|FAIL|TIMEOUT|REVISION_MISMATCH|TREE_MUTATED|SPAWN_ERROR>`, `${name}:stdout-sha256=<hex>`, `${name}:stderr-sha256=<hex>`. The summary carries at most the last 2000 characters of output. Return shape { claim, status, evidence, summary } matches the delivered fake verifier shape in packages/agentic-system/test/durable-backend-qa.test.js.

D7 — Backend proof: createBackendWorker({ strategy: createCodeActStrategy({ model, executor, maxTurns: 12, maxDurationMs: 30000 }), workspace, verifiers: [typecheck, tests] }). typecheck runs `node --check src/server.js`; tests runs `node --test test/`. The deterministic model emits CAPABILITY actions for AVOCapability.ACT (with edits), the two verification capabilities, EVALUATE and PROMOTE. It then returns return_result with a BackendWorkResult whose revision and artifacts are read from the ACT observation. The objective repository.revision is the fixture base commit sha.

D8 — QA proof: after Backend ACCEPT, a second createLocalGitWorkspace at the accepted sha serves as a read-only checkout. createQaWorker({ strategy: createCodeActStrategy(...deterministic model...), verifiers: [qa-behavior, qa-regression] }) uses local command verifiers with requireUnchangedTree true on that checkout, and QaCompletion must ACCEPT. The QA run goes through the delivered runBackendThenQaObjective or the equivalent delivered QA entry, not a new orchestration path.

D9 — Reproduction of the probe: the RB3 negative cases reuse the probe fixture shape, a temp git repository whose test/server.test.js fails until src/server.js returns { status: "ok" }. They assert that a model that edits nothing or edits an unrelated file never yields BackendCompletionAction.ACCEPT.

D10 — Evidence basis: executed BB-096 probe shows ACCEPT with PASS mutation/typecheck/tests on an unchanged repository whose real test exits 1. It also shows no process execution in agentic source, no agentic test using a Core model strategy, and no READY delivery plan owning BackendWorker/BackendCompletion or the README claim.
implementationSlices: L1 — Git workspace [RB1]: implement D1-D3. "RB1 ..." tests cover commit on edit (sha == HEAD, file content at `git show`), no-op edit → mutated false and no commit, each unsafe path class throws LOCAL_WORKSPACE_UNSAFE_PATH, revision mismatch throws, and source repository HEAD/branches/porcelain are unchanged after act and dispose.

L2 — Command verifier [RB2]: implement D4-D6. "RB2 ..." tests cover exit 0 → PASS with revision evidence, exit 1 → FAIL, HEAD != candidate.version → FAIL REVISION_MISMATCH with zero spawns, a command that writes a file → FAIL TREE_MUTATED, a `setInterval` process with timeoutMs 300 → INCONCLUSIVE TIMEOUT within 10s with the pid no longer alive, and an argument containing `; echo injected` passed literally.

L3 — Backend end-to-end [RB3]: implement D7 and D9 in the test file. "RB3 ..." tests cover the correct edit → BackendCompletionAction.ACCEPT with result.revision == worktree HEAD, mutation evidence afterRevision == HEAD, and the tests record containing `backend-tests:revision=<HEAD>`. The no-edit model and the unrelated-edit model each never ACCEPT. The source repository is unchanged.

L4 — QA end-to-end [RB4]: implement D8. "RB4 ..." tests cover QA ACCEPT on the accepted sha with both QA records PASS at that revision, a mutating QA command → QA not ACCEPT with TREE_MUTATED evidence, and a checkout at the base sha instead of the accepted sha → REVISION_MISMATCH.

L5 — Exports + docs [RB5]: export both factories from packages/agentic-system/src/index.js. The "RB5 ..." test asserts they are exported functions. Rewrite the README pipeline line so mutation/typecheck/tests evidence is produced by injected adapters, with delivered local git/command adapters. Document the adapters, their trust boundary (not a sandbox; BB-067) and the absence of a live provider (BB-066) in docs/living/system/agentic-application/state.md and capabilities.md. Then run test:agentic, verify:current-docs and npm test.

objectiveCoverage.objectiveCriterion: Specify a real local git workspace adapter whose ACT commits declared edits in an isolated detached worktree, carries the commit sha as candidate.version, rejects unsafe paths and no-op edits, and never changes the source repository HEAD or working tree.

Specify a real local command verifier that executes an argument-array process without a shell, is PASS only on exit 0, fails on revision mismatch or post-run tree mutation, terminates the process tree on timeout as INCONCLUSIVE, and binds evidence to the evaluated commit.

Specify an end-to-end proof that the delivered BackendWorker driven by a real Core CodeAct strategy with a deterministic model reaches ACCEPT only when the real commit makes the real test pass, and never ACCEPTs the executed probe shape (no or unrelated edit, failing test).

Specify an end-to-end proof that the delivered QaWorker verifies the accepted Backend commit through real command verifiers on a read-only checkout and fails when QA mutates the checkout or verifies a different revision.

Ground the design in the executed BB-096 probe, correct README and Living agentic docs so injected fixtures are distinguished from delivered local adapters, and produce an exact file-level plan, negative cases and executable verification for fresh Jev readiness.

negativeVerificationCases: An edit path that is absolute, contains "..", a drive letter or a ".git" segment throws LOCAL_WORKSPACE_UNSAFE_PATH and writes nothing.
An edit set that produces no diff returns mutated false, creates no commit and cannot lead to Backend ACCEPT.
ACT or verify when HEAD differs from candidate.version fails with a revision mismatch and spawns no verification process.
A verification process exiting non-zero yields FAIL; one exceeding timeoutMs yields INCONCLUSIVE TIMEOUT and its process tree is no longer alive.
A verification or QA command that changes HEAD or the working tree yields FAIL TREE_MUTATED even when it exits 0.
An argument containing shell metacharacters is passed literally and never interpreted by a shell.
The executed probe shape (model makes no edit or an unrelated edit while test/server.test.js fails) never yields BackendCompletionAction.ACCEPT.
QA run on a checkout of the base sha instead of the accepted Backend sha does not ACCEPT.
Any Backend or QA run leaves the source repository HEAD, branch list and porcelain status identical to before.
Any write to a forbiddenWrite path (Core, Oracle, backend-*.js, qa-*.js, existing fake-based tests, docs/blackboard) fails scope verification.
